passes.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished in-game room art direction concept for Workshop One in a Chinese prison industrial campus game.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved original campus master plan and exact layout/art reference, focus only on the red-boxed 一号车间; Image 2 is the current editor screenshot, use as current boundary/two south doors reference, DO NOT reproduce editor UI or red box.
Primary request: Redesign 一号车间 to restore the compact dense industrial workstation character of Image 1, at high visual clarity in the existing hand-painted game art style. Produce ONE polished final-effect concept image, a large landscape close-up of the whole room. This is a feasible modular sprite game scene, not a presentation board or asset sheet.
Camera: fixed high overhead 2.5D cutaway view with all architectural axes parallel to the screen, horizontal north/south walls and vertical east/west walls. NO diamond/isometric room, no perspective vanishing points. Show tops and short south-facing vertical faces of tables, machines and cabinets as in the supplied game. Show full room roof removed and a narrow outdoor tiled corridor in front, north/east/west continuous enclosure. Interior rectangle width:depth about 1.89:1, corresponding to 1360x720 world units. Ground tile size about40world units. Keep both south doors near 38% and76% of interior width. Clear continuous 120world-unit lane along inner south facade, central north-south aisle and transverse lane between table rows.
Room content: exactly FOUR large horizontal honey-brown wooden-top industrial workbenches, arranged in a clear 2-by-2 group. Each table visually approximately280world wide and120world deep ground footprint, visible front steel legs/dark slate-blue lower drawers. Tables occupy left/central bulk of room, right edge reserved for machinery strip. Sparse purposeful workpieces on table tops: first vise/hand tools and metal pieces, second small motor assembly and screwdriver, third copper wire coils and parts trays, fourth bench vise and finished housings. Props have crisp silhouettes and varied distinct work surfaces; no identical four copied tool arrangements.
North wall: dense but orderly run of worn blue-grey tool lockers, low spare-parts drawer cabinets, two compact bench-mounted industrial drill/press devices, an open bin shelf with rusted metal motor components, and one modest electrical control cabinet. Cabinet height believable relative to characters. Pipes run along wall with joints and a valve, one protected industrial light, a small shift board. West wall: narrow inward-facing storage racks with tools and boxes, low wooden stock crate at SW corner clear of door. East strip: two floor-standing drill presses at upper and lower positions, short shelf and three muted oil drums between them; narrow faded ochre safety marking around machinery floor. SE corner stock crates and a small wheeled cart, carefully outside both door paths. No lathe rows taking over central 4 tables; larger machine production belongs in Workshop Two.
Architecture: cream stone coping, worn warm beige plaster upper wall, dark slate-grey coarse lower masonry base differentiated from medical green tile and administrative blue panel. Tight clean mitered corners and continuous coping, subtle ageing with readable shapes. Two blue-grey steel south doorways OPEN with open door blades parked aside, short ground-level threshold, separate overhead lintel so centre passages appear completely clear. Small cream enamel sign centered above facade with exact readable Chinese text ONLY "一号车间". Avoid any other legible text, giant floor labels, HUD, arrows or editor markers.
Floor: muted warm grey-green square industrial tiles, restrained oil stains only under machinery, localized chips and worn table working positions, smooth readable quiet central aisles; NO muddy sand-noise everywhere, NO heavy blur.
People: three small full-body chibi orange-uniform workers at accessible sides of different workbenches and one compact dark grey uniform overseer in central aisle, same black-outline hand-painted cartoon character language as reference. Characters scaled to existing1.4 game proportion; reference adult sprite height86.8world units, tables must read roughly3.2character heights wide. Full bodies visible, do not hide workers inside tabletop geometry. No extra characters outside room.
Lighting: neutral diffuse soft daylight, restrained contact shadows close to feet and furniture; no shafts, bloom or long cast shadows. Palette honey wood, slate blue machines, charcoal iron, warm worn plaster, ochre small accents. High resolution edge definition, painted material texture with sparse abrasion, cohesive with provided references. Final concept should look like a finished game scene ready to be split into independent props, with a balanced inhabited production workshop, not empty oversized floor.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: final Workshop One room concept.
Image 1 is the edit target, preserve its complete artwork and scene composition. Image2 is ONLY the existing dark uniform overseer sprite sheet as character STYLE reference. Image3 is ONLY the existing orange worker sprite sheet as character STYLE reference. Do not copy sheets, frames, or UI into scene.
Make exactly two local corrections to Image1:
1. Move the entire LEFT SOUTH open steel doorway, including opening, blue leaves, ground threshold and frame, rightward so its centre is at38% of the interior width measured from the inside left wall to the inside right wall. It is currently around23%, which is wrong. Fill its old location with matching continuous cream coping, beige plaster, dark masonry base. Make the new opening same clear width as current left opening. The RIGHT SOUTH doorway is already correct, leave at76% width. Keep both lanes open with no horizontal blue rail across passable opening. Ground threshold lies flat.
2. Redraw only the FOUR existing humans (three orange workers and one overseer) using the small hand-painted chibi black-outline art proportions of images2 and3: larger head, compact body, expressive visible faces in gentle3/4 direction, full bodies and feet visible. Keep exact current feet positions and approximate current total heights so buildings and furniture do not change scale. Workers should face their table but heads can turn slightly to show recognisable cartoon faces. Overseer must use the exact stocky moustached balding character from image2, grey-brown jacket with red armband and brown trousers, existing worker orange clothing, no new outfits. Do not add characters.
Invariants: keep exactly four central workbenches in two rows/two columns, all table workpieces, all north cabinets, both east floor drill presses, western shelves, crates, tile floor, yellow safety zone, pipe valve, light, colour/materials, camera, rectangular screen-aligned plan, wall height, sign text exactly"一号车间", outdoor planters and whole canvas. No asset sheet, no inset, no captions, no red markup. Do not redesign the rest of the room. Crisp clean finished concept, no blur.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the existing final workshop concept edit target. Make ONLY the following tiny local correction to the TWO SOUTH DOOR OPENINGS. They are daytime OPEN entrances. Currently a blue horizontal door-like panel with yellow latch crosses the BACK of each opening. REMOVE this crossing blue panel and its latch entirely in BOTH openings. Replace just those pixels with continuous grey-green floor tiles visible THROUGH each opening, connecting inside workshop to exterior corridor with matching floor grid. Keep side jambs and the blue swung-open side leaves on both sides EXACTLY where they are. The top lintel may remain narrow, but the passage beneath must be visibly empty floor, completely unblocked with no horizontal blue object across it. Invariants: exact original canvas, all four worktables, all props, walls, cabinets, machines, 3 orange cartoon workers and 1 moustached overseer, both doorway x positions, nameplate text "一号车间", door width, contact shadows, tile material, everything else unchanged. Do NOT redesign the room or redraw characters. No extra UI or annotations.
